title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
claim: In 2022 Russia recorded 97% basic drinking water coverage, 89% basic sanitation coverage, 76% safely managed drinking water coverage, 61% safely managed sanitation coverage, and 0% open defecation.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s country dashboard publishes explicit indicator values for the target year.
ruler_attribution: Country-year welfare baseline; not uniquely attributable to Putin, but relevant to the ruler-period record.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF flags very high effort still needed to meet 2030 targets, so service coverage remains imperfect.

title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
claim: Russia’s child-health and schooling indicators were strong by 2022: DTP3 and MCV1 were both 97%, under-five mortality was 5 per 1,000 live births, neonatal mortality was 2, skilled birth attendance was 100% in 2020, lower-secondary completion was 100% in 2020, and upper-secondary completion was 91% in 2020.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s page provides explicit values drawn from internationally comparable data series.
period_fit: Mostly 2022, with clearly labeled adjacent-year measures where shown on the page.
ruler_attribution: Baseline and outcome context; attribution to Putin is indirect and should be paired with policy evidence.
contrary_evidence: The same page marks several education and health targets as still requiring effort, so the picture is not uniformly strong.

title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
claim: Russia reported 0% children in extreme poverty in 2022, 12% of children below the national poverty line in 2020, and 100% child coverage by social protection floors/systems in 2020.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s dashboard summarizes comparable child-poverty and social-protection indicators with explicit values and years.
period_fit: Mostly 2022, with adjacent-year child-poverty and social-protection indicators explicitly labeled on the page.
ruler_attribution: Baseline/outcome context; social protection coverage may reflect inherited systems as well as 2022 policy choices.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard also shows that child-poverty and social-protection data are incomplete in some adjacent dimensions, so this should not be over-read as comprehensive welfare success.

title: Russian Federation health system information
publisher: WHO European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies
claim: The Russian Federation has universal health coverage with free care in state and municipal facilities, but quality and availability vary widely by region; prescriptions usually require patient payment except for some protected groups, and since 2019 reforms have focused on improving primary care access, especially in rural areas.
source_confidence_reason: The Observatory is a specialist WHO-affiliated health-system reference and the claims are explicit on the page.
period_fit: System description is stable context for 2022, not a one-off event.
ruler_attribution: System-level context rather than direct ruler attribution; useful for judging what feasible improvements Putin could have delivered.
contrary_evidence: The same source says service quality and availability vary widely by region, which limits any claim of uniform access.

title: Systematic Country Diagnostic for the Russian Federation: Pathways to Inclusive Growth
claim: The World Bank said Russia needed deeper human-capital gains and better public services, because life expectancy, especially for men, was low and regional and socioeconomic health differences were large; it also said social assistance should be focused more on the most vulnerable, and that pensions had a low adequacy problem.
source_confidence_reason: The diagnostic is a World Bank synthesis of policy-relevant evidence and states the conclusions directly.
period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline context, useful for judging 2022 ruler-period change and feasible policy space.
ruler_attribution: Context and constraint evidence, not direct proof of 2022 action.
contrary_evidence: This is a diagnostic, so it identifies problems and policy needs rather than demonstrating that Putin corrected them in 2022.

title: Russia's Economic Recovery Gathers Pace, Says New World Bank Report
claim: The World Bank said Russia spent over 3% of GDP, or about $30 billion per year, on social-assistance programs, and that this spending was more than three times the combined income deficit of all poor families before transfers.
source_confidence_reason: A World Bank press release summarizing a country report with explicit quantitative findings.
period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline, relevant for judging whether 2022 actions built on or merely inherited an expensive safety net.
ruler_attribution: Baseline and policy-capacity context rather than direct 2022 attribution.
contrary_evidence: The same report says a targeted program could reduce poverty faster and at lower fiscal cost, implying the existing system was not fully efficient.

title: COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Policy Response to Protecting the Poorest and Most Vulnerable in Russia
claim: The World Bank warned that families with children could see poverty rise by 2 or more percentage points, that central and north-western federal districts could see poverty increases twice as large as other regions, and that expanded child allowances and social-assistance measures could partly offset the shock.
source_confidence_reason: The page gives explicit scenario estimates and identifies the mitigation policies.
period_fit: Pre-2022 crisis policy context that carried into the target year.
ruler_attribution: Policy-response context; the measures were part of the inherited and ongoing welfare architecture rather than uniquely a 2022 Putin innovation.
contrary_evidence: The same source says poorer households, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities were especially exposed, showing substantial residual vulnerability.

title: COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Policy Response to Addressing Learning Gaps and Inequalities in Russia
claim: The World Bank said most children, and especially poor children, could lose up to six months of learning from school disruptions, with under-represented students more likely to drop out or finish with lower qualifications and with widened inequity in learning outcomes.
source_confidence_reason: The World Bank page is explicit about the education shock and distributional effects.
period_fit: Pandemic-era background that shaped 2022 human-development outcomes.
ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than direct 2022 Putin attribution; useful because the government’s response had to operate under these conditions.
contrary_evidence: The page notes some distance learning existed, so the loss was not total or uniform.

title: New Skills Development Key to Further Improving Students’ Learning Outcomes, Says World Bank Report
claim: The World Bank reported that 38% of Russian schools lacked workshops, 46% lacked scientific laboratories, and 77% lacked dedicated spaces for integrated lessons that support teamwork and skill development.
source_confidence_reason: The press release gives direct numeric findings from the underlying report.
period_fit: Pre-2022 system-quality context relevant to 2022 outcomes.
ruler_attribution: Context for inherited constraints; not direct evidence of 2022 Putin action.
contrary_evidence: The report also says Russian students are often strong academically, so the issue is quality and modern skills, not universal failure.

title: Russian Federation - Demographic and socioeconomic outcome data in UNICEF country profile
claim: Russia’s 2022 child welfare profile still showed major service needs despite strong averages, including very high effort required to hit water and sanitation targets and only partial child-poverty progress in the 2020-2022 data series.
source_confidence_reason: Same UNICEF country dashboard; this claim synthesizes the table’s explicit target-effort labels rather than drawing a new inference.
period_fit: 2022 target-year fit is explicit on the page.
ruler_attribution: Context, not direct attribution; helpful for interpreting the baseline-adjusted welfare record.
contrary_evidence: The same page marks some targets as already met, so the record is mixed rather than uniformly poor.

title: Russian Federation
claim: WHO’s country profile classifies Russia as high income, shows current health expenditure at 7.39% of GDP in 2021, and tracks under-five mortality for 2022 alongside life-expectancy indicators.
source_confidence_reason: WHO country data page with explicit country classification and tracked indicators; the page is stronger on baseline context than on ruler attribution.
period_fit: The page mixes 2021 and 2022 indicators but is clearly in the target-period neighborhood.
ruler_attribution: Baseline context only.
contrary_evidence: The page does not itself show Putin-specific policy choices, so it should not be over-attributed.

title: Putin orders benefit payments for people arriving in Russia from Ukraine
claim: Putin signed a decree introducing financial benefits for people who left Ukrainian territory for Russia, including monthly pension payments of 10,000 roubles for people forced to leave Ukraine, disability support, and a one-off payment for pregnant women.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable reporting and the page states the decree’s terms explicitly, though it is a syndicated host page.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin action, but the policy was tied to people displaced from Ukraine rather than the general Russian population.
contrary_evidence: The same report links the benefit policy to Russia-backed territorial claims in Ukraine, so the measure may also have a strategic or political purpose.

title: Russia's 2022 economic fall seen in lower incomes, slumping consumer demand
claim: Rosstat data reported by Reuters showed real disposable incomes fell 1% in 2022, retail sales slumped 6.7%, and unemployment stayed at a record low 3.7% in December.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable and the article reports specific Rosstat figures on household income and demand.
ruler_attribution: Outcome context for the Putin period; not a pure policy attribution by itself.
contrary_evidence: The same article says unemployment remained very low, so the welfare picture is mixed rather than uniformly deteriorating.

title: Russian unemployment rate hits record low, economic data paints mixed picture
claim: Reuters reported that Rosstat said real wages in Russia fell 3.2% year on year in July and that car production shrank 69% in annual terms, showing significant sectoral strain even with low unemployment.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable and the article reports specific official data points with concrete figures.
ruler_attribution: Outcome context for the Putin period; not full causal attribution by itself.
contrary_evidence: The same article says unemployment was still at a record low, so the economy was not uniformly in collapse.

title: Russia says budget deficit hit 2.3% of GDP in 2022
claim: Russia recorded a 2022 budget deficit of 2.3% of GDP and had to draw on its rainy-day fund while diverting more funds toward security and defence.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports official fiscal data and the fiscal tradeoff is explicit on the page.
ruler_attribution: Useful for judging 2022 fiscal capacity and tradeoffs under Putin.
contrary_evidence: A deficit is not automatically mismanagement; the same report says it reflected war-related spending pressures.

title: Putin says Russia will post budget surplus this year, GDP to decline around 2%
claim: Putin said budget spending was up 20% on the previous year, predicted only about a 2% GDP decline, and acknowledged that economic hardships remained for many Russians.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters-transmitted reporting on a Putin speech, with explicit numerical claims and a clear acknowledgment of hardship.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin rhetoric and self-assessment, though it remains self-serving official speech evidence.
contrary_evidence: This is self-reporting by Putin, so it should be weighed against independent outcome evidence rather than taken at face value.

title: World Economic Outlook Report 10/11/2022
claim: The IMF said Russia’s invasion of Ukraine was part of the broader cost-of-living crisis weighing on the outlook and that fiscal policy should help alleviate cost-of-living pressures while keeping policy sufficiently tight.
source_confidence_reason: The IMF report directly states the macro policy guidance and the role of the war in the cost-of-living crisis.
ruler_attribution: Context rather than direct Putin attribution; relevant to the shock environment he had to manage.
contrary_evidence: The IMF’s advice is generic across countries, so it does not by itself prove good or bad Russian implementation.

title: Human Development Report 2021-22
claim: UNDP said the ongoing pandemic had reversed human development in almost every country and that war in Ukraine and elsewhere had created more human suffering and a worldwide cost-of-living crisis.
source_confidence_reason: UNDP’s report states the macro-human-development context directly and dates it clearly.
ruler_attribution: Context only, not a direct Putin-policy finding.
contrary_evidence: The report is global and not Russia-specific, so it should be used only as background, not as ruler-level proof.

title: 2022 Education Finance Watch
claim: The report says the Covid-19 pandemic exacerbated the global learning crisis and that the 2022 edition analyzes education financing across 2020, 2021, and 2022 using the latest data available as of May 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Joint UNESCO/World Bank/UIS publication with explicit summary language, but it is global rather than Russia-specific.
ruler_attribution: Context only.
contrary_evidence: Because it is global, it should not be over-read as direct evidence about Russia’s government choices.

title: Reimbursable Advisory Services in Russia
claim: The World Bank’s Russia advisory platform describes its health work as expanding access to affordable health care, and its social-protection work as covering safety nets, pensions, labor programs, and delivery systems such as targeting, payments, governance, monitoring, and evaluation.
source_confidence_reason: The page is a World Bank description of its Russia-facing advisory portfolio, useful for policy context and implementation design.
period_fit: Still relevant to the 2022 institutional environment.
ruler_attribution: Context only; it shows what policy tools existed, not that Putin used them well.
contrary_evidence: This is an advisory-program page, so it is weaker on actual 2022 delivery outcomes than on policy capacity.

title: Russian Federation

source_confidence_reason: WHO country data are authoritative baseline indicators, though this page is more descriptive than policy-attributive.
period_fit: Mixed 2021-2022 indicator neighborhood, useful as baseline context.
ruler_attribution: Baseline context only, not direct Putin attribution.
contrary_evidence: The page does not itself identify ruler-specific policy choices or service-quality changes in 2022.

title: Росстат представляет данные о естественном движении населения в декабре 2022 года
claim: Rosstat reported that in 2022 Russia recorded 1,306,162 births, 1,905,778 deaths, and a natural decrease of 599,616 people, with deaths down 22.1 percent from 2021.
source_confidence_reason: Primary official statistics release with precise annual demographic totals.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; the figures are official outcomes of the state statistical system and wartime context rather than a personal decree
contrary_evidence: The release also shows continued population decline despite the improvement versus 2021.

title: Отчет о ходе реализации государственной программы Российской Федерации Развитие здравоохранения за 2022 год

source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry PDF opened directly; the claim comes from the report's first-page summary table.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; this is ministry implementation inside a Putin-era program framework rather than a personal act
contrary_evidence: The report is self-reporting and does not by itself prove real-world health gains.

title: Instructions following a meeting on socioeconomic support for regions
claim: Putin approved instructions to assess unemployed families' financial status so social support could be provided, improve access to support for families with children whose income had fallen, add extra indexation for pensions, social benefits and wages at state and municipal organizations, raise the minimum wage and subsistence minimum, and allocate federal funds to reduce poverty and income inequality in 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instructions published on the Kremlin site with concrete 2022 policy mandates.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin instruction, with implementation delegated to the government and regions.
contrary_evidence: The same instructions were largely crisis-response measures under war and sanctions pressure, not evidence of preplanned prosperity building.

title: Government indexed pensions, the subsistence minimum and the minimum wage by 10%
claim: The Russian government said that from 1 June 2022 insurance pensions for non-working pensioners, the subsistence minimum and the minimum wage would all rise by 10%, and that the decision was taken on Putin's instruction.
locator: government announcement headline and decree summary
source_confidence_reason: Formal government decree summary with explicit rate change and attribution to Putin's instruction.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin-linked policy direction, implemented through the government.
contrary_evidence: A flat indexation compensates only partly for inflation and does not by itself show lasting welfare improvement.

title: Government meeting: new monthly benefits for children aged 8-17 from low-income families
claim: The government said it had started paying new monthly benefits for children aged 8-17 in low-income families on Putin's instruction, with more than 2.5 million applications covering 3.5 million children and average monthly payments of 6,000 to 12,000 roubles.
source_confidence_reason: Official government announcement with concrete uptake and payment details tied to a presidential instruction.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin instruction, operationalized through government payment systems.
contrary_evidence: The program is targeted to low-income families and does not by itself resolve broader child poverty or service-quality problems.

title: Government allocated over 35.3 billion roubles for families with children
claim: The government said more than 35.3 billion roubles would be additionally sent to regions for monthly payments to low-income and large families with children.
locator: government news summary on 11 October 2022 directives
source_confidence_reason: Official budget-allocation announcement with a specific funding amount and beneficiary group.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but clear Putin-period attribution through the federal executive branch.
contrary_evidence: Extra transfers can cushion hardship without proving durable gains in underlying living standards.

title: Government meeting: payments to hero mothers and parental glory recipients
claim: The government said President Putin revived the Soviet-era Hero Mother title with a 1 million rouble payment, raised the Order of Parental Glory payment to 500,000 roubles, and added 200,000 roubles for the Parental Glory medal.
source_confidence_reason: Official government meeting summary with explicit benefit terms and direct presidential initiative.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin-linked family-policy decision.
contrary_evidence: This is pro-natalist spending, not a broad measure of child well-being or service quality.

title: Government supports school meals and child-health measures
claim: By presidential instruction, the government said primary-school pupils receive free hot meals and that almost 59 billion roubles was spent in 2022, with nearly 188 billion roubles allocated for 2022-2024; the same package included anti-obesity measures and public posting of school meal information.
source_confidence_reason: Official government announcement with spending figures and implementation details.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but substantial Putin-period policy attribution through the executive branch.
contrary_evidence: The policy is school-specific and does not by itself establish broader system quality or equity.

title: Government says at least 1,300 new schools will be built
claim: The government said that 324 new kindergartens had opened, about 100 new schools had opened, and that at least 1,300 new secondary schools would be built by 2025; it also said more than 4,000 school buses had been purchased and free hot meals were being provided to primary school students.
source_confidence_reason: Official implementation summary with concrete delivery numbers and an explicit state program frame.
period_fit: Target-period 2022, with implementation carried over from Putin-era education policy.
ruler_attribution: Indirect ruler attribution through the federal executive and presidential initiative.
contrary_evidence: The target extends beyond 2022 and combines older pipeline projects with new construction, so attribution to the single year is partial.

title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation

title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
claim: UNICEF's Russia dashboard reports 97% DTP3 immunization and 97% measles-first-dose coverage in 2022, 100% skilled birth attendance in 2020, maternal mortality of 14 per 100,000 live births in 2020, under-five mortality of 5 per 1,000 in 2021, and neonatal mortality of 2 per 1,000 in 2021.

ruler_attribution: Indirect system/outcome evidence; attribution to Putin is partial and mediated by long-run health institutions.
contrary_evidence: These are outcome indicators rather than proof of 2022 policy improvement, and several values predate 2022 exactly.

title: Russian Federation (RUS) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
claim: UNICEF's Russia country page reports an under-five mortality rate of 5 deaths per 1,000 live births, an infant mortality rate of 4, a neonatal mortality rate of 2, and a 2022 under-five total of 6,759 deaths.

period_fit: Target-period outcome context with 2022 values and immediately adjacent years.
ruler_attribution: Indirect baseline/outcome evidence; not a direct policy act.
contrary_evidence: Mortality remains low by international standards but not exceptional, and the page does not isolate Putin-period causal contribution.

title: Russian Federation (RUS) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
claim: UNICEF's Russia country page reports 100% birth registration, 91% upper-secondary completion in 2020, 100% primary and lower-secondary completion in 2020, and 93% participation in organized early learning in 2019.

ruler_attribution: Indirect system evidence; largely inherited and institution-mediated.

title: Russian Federation (RUS) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality

ruler_attribution: Indirect baseline/outcome evidence rather than direct Putin action.

title: Russian Federation
claim: WHO's Russia country page reports current health expenditure at 7.39% of GDP, doctor density at 51.1 per 10,000 population, and nursing and midwifery density at 70.4 per 10,000 population in 2022.

title: Rosstat представляет данные о естественном движении населения в декабре 2022 года
claim: Rosstat reported that in 2022 Russia had 1,306,162 births, 1,905,778 deaths, and a natural decrease of 599,616 people, with deaths down 22.1% from 2021 and infant mortality down 17.7% in December 2022 compared with December 2021.
source_confidence_reason: Primary national statistics release with explicit year-end figures and year-on-year comparisons.
ruler_attribution: Indirect demographic outcome evidence; strongly confounded by pandemic and other structural factors.
contrary_evidence: The country still recorded a large natural population decrease, so lower deaths did not translate into broad demographic improvement.
